architecture.polyphony_mode: monophonic, or two voices in DUO keyboard mode. The specifications say 'Multiphonic', the ARP term for duophonic.
architecture.summary: A fully normalled modular. 3 VCOs (each switchable to LFO range, VCO2 and VCO3 syncable to VCO1) plus a noise generator and a ring modulator feed a 4-pole low-pass VCF through five attenuator sliders. The VCF and the ring modulator feed a VCA in parallel, and VCF and VCA outputs are then blended in a two-channel mixer, panned, sent through reverb and out in stereo. Two envelope generators (AR and ADSR) are triggered from the keyboard, the sample and hold clock, or external gate and trigger jacks. A dedicated LFO with delayed vibrato, a preamp and envelope follower, a sample and hold with an internal clock, an electronic switch, a voltage processor (two inverting summers and a lag processor) and a 4-way mult complete the set. Every pre-wired connection has a jack above its slider that breaks the normal when a plug is inserted.

modules.name: Keyboard interface
modules.description: Turns incoming MIDI into pitch CV, gate and trigger. MONO plays one voice; DUO splits the held notes so the lowest drives the main keyboard CV and the highest drives the UPPER VOICE output. REPEAT and TRIG MODE decide how triggers are generated. There is no physical keyboard on this model; the section is driven over MIDI or USB.

modules.name: Portamento
modules.description: Slews the keyboard CV so one pitch slides to the next. Switched on by the panel switch, momentarily by the MOMEN button, or by a footswitch on the rear.

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Oscillator 1
modules.description: Analogue VCO. The AUDIO/LF switch moves it between four audio ranges and four sub-audio ranges; in LF it becomes an LFO and keyboard control is disabled automatically. Outputs sawtooth and pulse.

frequency_hz.note: specifications give 0.03 Hz to 40 kHz across four overlapping ranges for the three VCOs together

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Oscillator 2
modules.description: Analogue VCO. The AUDIO/LF switch moves it between four audio ranges and four sub-audio ranges; in LF it becomes an LFO and keyboard control is disabled automatically. Outputs triangle, sawtooth, sine and pulse, all simultaneously available. SYNC locks it to VCO1 so the pair behaves as one oscillator following VCO1's frequency.

frequency_hz.note: specifications give 0.03 Hz to 40 kHz across four overlapping ranges for the three VCOs together

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Oscillator 3
modules.description: Analogue VCO. The AUDIO/LF switch moves it between four audio ranges and four sub-audio ranges; in LF it becomes an LFO and keyboard control is disabled automatically. Outputs triangle, sawtooth, sine and pulse, all simultaneously available. SYNC locks it to VCO1 so the pair behaves as one oscillator following VCO1's frequency.

frequency_hz.note: specifications give 0.03 Hz to 40 kHz across four overlapping ranges for the three VCOs together

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Filter / Resonator
modules.description: 4-pole low-pass filter with variable cutoff and resonance. A switch picks between two filter circuits, the 4012 and the 4072. Five audio attenuators and three control attenuators feed it.

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Amplifier
modules.description: Amplifier sitting in parallel with the VCF rather than after it; both are blended in the mixer. At maximum gain it passes signal at unity; at minimum it passes nothing. INITIAL GAIN sets the standing gain, and the two control inputs add to it, one linear and one exponential.

modules.name: AR Envelope Generator
modules.description: Attack and release transient generator, fired by the gate or trigger chosen at its routing switch or by the MANUAL button. TIME FACTOR scales both times.

modules.name: ADSR Envelope Generator
modules.description: Four-stage transient generator, fired by the gate or trigger chosen at its routing switch or by the MANUAL button. TIME FACTOR scales the times.

modules.name: Envelope trigger routing
modules.description: Selects what fires the envelopes. Each generator has a three-position routing switch choosing the pre-wired S/H CLOCK, the GATE IN jack or the TRIG IN jack, and the manual says the chosen signal is passed on to the ADSR as well. The keyboard gate and trigger and the MANUAL buttons also reach the envelopes.

modules.name: Mixer
modules.description: Two attenuators, pre-wired from the VCF and the VCA, summed to one signal which is then panned into the stereo output. The summed signal also feeds the reverb over a separate pre-wired connection that the POST-MIXER jack does not break.

modules.name: Reverb
modules.description: Stereo reverb fed from the mixer sum, with its own left and right level sliders and two input jacks that sum extra signal hard left and hard right. Digital on the 2600; the BLUE MARVIN edition has a real spring tank.

modules.name: Stereo output
modules.description: Final left and right outputs on parallel 1/4-inch and 3.5 mm jacks, plus the headphone amplifier, which is fed from the mixer output.

modules.name: Low Frequency Oscillator
modules.description: Dedicated LFO intended to work with the keyboard. Sawtooth, square and sine are all available at once on separate jacks; the sine is pre-wired to VCO1 and is the one that carries the vibrato delay and depth.

modules.name: Noise Generator
modules.description: Noise source sweepable through low frequency, pink and white with one slider, followed by a level slider.

modules.name: Ring Modulator
modules.description: Voltage multiplier combining two inputs. Pre-wired from VCO1 sawtooth and VCO2 sine; each input jack blends an external signal with the pre-wired one rather than replacing it, and the adjacent slider sets the combined gain. An AUDIO/DC switch optimises the VCO1 path for audio or control voltages.

modules.name: Preamp
modules.description: Switchable-gain preamp bringing an external signal up to synth level, in three ranges of x10, x100 and x1000 (20, 40 and 60 dB). Pre-wired into the envelope follower.

modules.name: Envelope Follower
modules.description: Produces a control voltage tracking the average amplitude of its input. Fed from the preamp over a pre-wired connection, or directly through its own input, which blends rather than replaces. Its output has no pre-wired destination anywhere in the synth, so it needs a cable.

modules.name: Sample & Hold
modules.description: Samples its input on each clock tick and holds the value until the next, turning a smooth signal into a stepped one. Pre-wired from the noise generator, which makes it a random voltage source by default. Runs on its own internal clock unless EXT CLK IN is patched, which disables the internal clock and the RATE slider with it.

modules.name: Electronic Switch
modules.description: Bidirectional two-way switch clocked by the sample and hold internal clock. It can alternate one input at C between outputs A and B, or alternate the C output between two inputs at A and B.

modules.name: Inverter 1
modules.description: Sums four inputs and inverts the result. A +10 V input leaves as -10 V; audio leaves with its phase reversed. Three of the four inputs have attenuator sliders.

modules.name: Inverter 2
modules.description: Sums two inputs and inverts the result.

modules.name: Lag Processor
modules.description: Slows down sudden changes in the input voltage by an amount set by its slider. On audio it behaves as a low-pass filter, rolling off treble as the lag increases.

modules.name: Mult
modules.description: Four jacks wired in parallel, usable in any combination of inputs and outputs, for splitting one signal to several destinations or passively combining several.

parameters.label: INITIAL OSCILLATOR FREQUENCY

physical.taper: approximately logarithmic, about one decade per marked division

parameters.function: Coarse operating frequency. The scale is marked in four audio decades (10 Hz, 100 Hz, 1 kHz, 10 kHz) and, for LF mode, four sub-audio ones (.03, .3, 3.0, 30 Hz). The ranges overlap, so the marks locate a region rather than switch between fixed bands.

parameters.label: FINE TUNE
parameters.function: Trims the frequency up or down from the coarse setting. The span is not stated.

parameters.label: PULSE WIDTH
parameters.function: Duty cycle of the pulse output, marked 10%, 50% and 90%. This is the standing width before any PWM.

parameters.label: AUDIO (KYBD ON) / LF (KYBD OFF)

physical.note: end points read from the panel scale; the manual gives no measured range

parameters.function: Coarse cutoff, marked at 10 Hz, 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz.

parameters.label: FINE TUNE
parameters.function: Trims the cutoff up or down from the coarse setting.

parameters.label: RESONANCE
parameters.function: Filter Q. At MAX the response around cutoff becomes sharp and the filter rings in response to pulses passing through it. The manual stops short of saying it self-oscillates.

parameters.label: MODE (4012 / 4072)
parameters.function: Chooses between two filter circuits. The manual's description of them is garbled: it calls the 4012 the original design with a 16 Hz maximum cutoff and the 4072 a lower maximum at 11 Hz, which cannot be right for a filter whose panel is marked to 10 kHz. Read as 16 kHz and 11 kHz.
parameters.note: The kHz reading is an inference from the panel scale and from the two circuits being audio filters.

parameters.label: ATTACK TIME
parameters.function: Time to rise to the fixed peak when a key is pressed or a gate or trigger arrives.

parameters.label: RELEASE TIME
parameters.function: Fall time after the key or the gate is released.

parameters.label: MANUAL

parameters.label: TIME FACTOR (x2 / x1 / x0.5)
parameters.function: Multiplies the whole envelope's timing.

parameters.label: ROUTING SWITCH
parameters.function: Chooses what fires the envelope: the pre-wired S/H CLOCK, the GATE IN jack or the TRIG IN jack. The manual adds that the chosen signal is passed on to the ADSR generator as well.

parameters.label: DECAY TIME

parameters.label: REL TIME
parameters.function: Fall time after the key or the gate is released.

parameters.label: MANUAL
parameters.function: Produces a gate by hand, firing both the AR and the ADSR. The manual lists a MANUAL button under both generators; the panel has one button in the AR block and one in the ADSR block.

parameters.label: ROUTING SWITCH
parameters.function: Chooses what fires the envelope: the pre-wired S/H CLOCK, the GATE IN jack or the TRIG IN jack.

parameters.label: INITIAL GAIN
parameters.function: Standing gain of the VCA before any control voltage is added. At maximum the VCA passes signal at unity gain; at minimum it passes nothing.

parameters.label: PAN
parameters.function: Places the summed mixer signal in the stereo field before the final output.

parameters.label: REVERB L
parameters.function: Left reverb level. Unnumbered on the panel; listed in the specifications as one of the mixer and reverb sliders.

parameters.label: REVERB R
parameters.function: Right reverb level. Unnumbered on the panel; listed in the specifications as one of the mixer and reverb sliders.

parameters.label: PHONES level
parameters.function: Headphone volume. The headphone feed is taken from the mixer output.

parameters.label: POWER
parameters.function: Turns the synthesizer on and off. Make the connections before switching on.

parameters.label: VOICE MODE (MONO / DUO)
parameters.function: MONO plays one voice at a time. DUO plays two: the main keyboard CV and the separate UPPER VOICE output.

parameters.label: REPEAT (KYBD / OFF / AUTO)
parameters.function: How triggers are generated. KYBD sends repeating trigger pulses for as long as a key is held. AUTO sends a stream of triggers at the LFO rate. OFF gives one trigger per key press, which is normal keyboard behaviour.

parameters.label: TRIG MODE (SINGLE / MULT)
parameters.function: SINGLE generates a trigger only when a key is played with no other key down, which is legato behaviour. MULT generates a trigger on every key press even while other keys are held.

parameters.label: ON / OFF
parameters.function: Turns portamento on or off.

parameters.label: MOMEN
parameters.function: Turns portamento on for as long as the button is held.

parameters.label: MAX / MIN
parameters.function: Strength of the portamento. MAX is the most gradual glide.

parameters.label: LFO SPEED
parameters.function: Base rate of the LFO, and therefore of the AUTO repeat trigger stream.

parameters.label: VIB DELAY

parameters.label: VIB DEPTH

parameters.label: RANGE (x1000 / x100 / x10)

parameters.label: GAIN

indicators.label: Slider LEDs
indicators.function: Every slider cap carries a lit LED. The colour is fixed per slider and is not adjustable; the rear LED knob changes brightness only. See led_legend for what the colours appear to encode, and the led_colour field on each parameter for the observed colour of that slider.

led_legend.rule: A slider's LED takes the colour of the module the signal in it comes from. A module's own sliders (its frequency, its envelope times, its gain) carry that module's colour, and an attenuator slider for a pre-wired input carries the colour of the source at the other end. So the five VCF audio sliders read green, blue, green, blue, green from left to right, matching ring modulator, VCO1, VCO2, VCO3 and noise, and the pattern repeats wherever those sources appear.

colours.meaning: VCO 2, noise generator, ring modulator, reverb
the two envelope generators, AR and ADSR
the clock and modulation sources: LFO and sample and hold
the signal-path and control blocks: VCF, VCA, mixer, keyboard CV, portamento, preamp, envelope follower, voltage processor

exceptions: The ring modulator's two sliders are both green although their sources are VCO1 (blue) and VCO2 (green). This fits the rule rather than breaking it: the manual says those sliders set the gain of the combined pre-wired and patched signal, so they are the module's own gain controls, not per-source attenuators.
VCO1 and VCO3 share blue, so colour distinguishes signal families rather than individual modules.
led_legend.note: Read off the front panel photograph. The manual documents the LEDs only as something whose brightness the rear knob controls; it contains no colour legend at all, and neither do the specifications. Every observation here is consistent, but the rule itself is a reading, not a documented fact.

The switching rate of the electronic switch is set by the sample and hold internal clock. The clock gates the switch rather than passing through it; modelled as a connection for want of a clock-control node.

behaviours.name: Pre-wiring and normalling
behaviours.rule: Every pre-wired connection is drawn on the panel as an orange line ending in a labelled box. Directly above the box is a jack, and directly above that a slider. The slider attenuates whatever reaches that input. Inserting a plug into the jack breaks the factory connection and substitutes the patched signal, which the slider then attenuates instead. The ring modulator and envelope follower inputs are the exceptions: they blend with the pre-wired signal rather than replacing it.

behaviours.name: Parallel VCF and VCA
behaviours.rule: Unlike a conventional subtractive voice, the VCA does not sit after the filter. The VCF feeds the VCA, but the mixer takes both the VCF output and the VCA output as separate channels, so the two are blended rather than cascaded. Dialling the mixer's VCF channel up gives unshaped filter output alongside the amplitude-shaped path.

behaviours.name: VCO as LFO
behaviours.rule: Moving a VCO's AUDIO/LF switch to LF shifts all four frequency ranges down to 0.03, 0.3, 3.0 and 30 Hz and disables keyboard control automatically. The oscillator keeps all of its outputs, so it becomes a multi-waveform modulation source with the same panel controls.

behaviours.name: Envelope triggering
behaviours.rule: Each envelope has a three-way routing switch choosing the pre-wired S/H CLOCK, the GATE IN jack or the TRIG IN jack, and a MANUAL button that fires both generators by hand. The keyboard's own gate and trigger also reach them. How these sources combine, and whether the routing switch replaces the keyboard or sits alongside it, is not stated.

behaviours.name: Keyboard repeat and trigger modes
behaviours.rule: REPEAT set to KYBD sends repeating triggers while a key is held; AUTO sends a stream at the LFO rate; OFF gives one trigger per press. Independently, TRIG MODE SINGLE only triggers when no other key is held (legato), while MULT triggers on every press. Together they decide whether held notes re-fire the envelopes.

behaviours.name: Duophonic keyboard
behaviours.rule: In DUO mode the keyboard produces two control voltages: the main KYBD CV and the UPPER VOICE output for the highest note held. The rear INTERVAL LATCH footswitch freezes the interval between the two so that further single notes keep it. Only the main CV is pre-wired to the oscillators; using the second voice means patching UPPER VOICE somewhere.

behaviours.name: Sample and hold clocking
behaviours.rule: The internal clock drives the sampling, the electronic switch's alternation, and, through the envelope routing switches, the envelopes. Patching EXT CLK IN disables the internal clock entirely, which also makes the RATE slider inert.

behaviours.name: Voltage processor summing
behaviours.rule: Inverter 1 sums its four inputs and inverts the result, so +10 V in gives -10 V out and audio comes out 180 degrees out of phase. Inverter 2 does the same for two inputs. The lag processor slews its input; on audio that reads as a low-pass filter. None of the three has a pre-wired destination, so the voltage processor only does anything when patched.

behaviours.name: Mult is passive
behaviours.rule: The four MULT jacks are wired directly together with no buffering, so they work in any combination of inputs and outputs. Loading and mixing behave as passive parallel connections do: several sources joined at a mult sum and interact rather than staying independent.

behaviours.name: Envelope times
behaviours.rule: Both generators output 0 to +10 V. The TIME FACTOR switch multiplies the whole envelope's timing by 0.5, 1 or 2. No absolute times in seconds are given anywhere in the manual or specifications.

behaviours.name: Composite oscillator outputs
behaviours.rule: The manual states that each VCO's PULSE output can also be used to mix in a signal from another section: the LFO for VCO1, the noise generator for VCO2, the ADSR for VCO3. This reads as the modulation source appearing at the pulse jack alongside the oscillator, but the mechanism is not explained and no slider is identified.

behaviours.name: Electronic switch crosspoints
behaviours.rule: The three terminals are bidirectional. Either C is the input and the signal alternates between the A and B outputs, or A and B are two inputs and C alternates between them. The alternation rate is the sample and hold internal clock, so it follows the RATE slider unless EXT CLK IN is patched. The crosspoints are internal to the module and so do not appear in connections.

behaviours.name: LFO vibrato delay
behaviours.rule: VIB DELAY sets how long the sine takes to fade in and VIB DEPTH its intensity. The manual describes both as acting on the delayed sine, and describes the LFO (SINE) DELAYED jack as a delayed copy of the LFO's pre-wired sine output. Whether the pre-wire to VCO1 carries the delayed sine or the plain one is therefore unclear; this file wires the plain sine to VCO1 and exposes the delayed copy at the jack.

behaviours.name: Pan and the stereo output
behaviours.rule: The mixer sum passes through PAN into the left and right outputs, and separately into the reverb, whose left and right levels are set by their own sliders and summed into the same outputs. The POST-MIXER jack breaks the feed into PAN but not the feed into the reverb, so patching it leaves the reverb still hearing the mixer.

source_inconsistencies: Item 12 describes the 4012 as having a 16 Hz maximum cutoff and the 4072 an 11 Hz maximum. Both figures must be kHz for a filter whose panel is marked to 10 kHz.
The specifications list SYNC as 'VCO 2 / 3 only' under controls and 'VCO 1 / 2 only' under switches. Item 4 and the panel agree it is on VCO2 and VCO3.
The specifications count 11 FM control jacks; the panel has twelve, four on each VCO.
The specifications count one GATE IN jack; the manual numbers two, items 24 and 31, and the panel has two.
The LFO sawtooth output is item 57 and is marked SAW on the panel, but the specifications call it triangle.
Item 79 says the -10 V input 'attenuates the input signal by 10 V', which is not what an attenuator does. The panel and specifications treat it as a -10 V source input with a gain slider.
Items 20 and 33 are the same routing switch description repeated for both generators, each saying the chosen signal is also routed to the ADSR, which cannot be true of the ADSR's own switch.
Item 5 says the type of waveform is shown by the silk-screening 'depending on the specific VCO in use', without saying that VCO1 has only two outputs while VCO2 and VCO3 have four.
The manual is titled Quick Start Guide throughout but is a full controls manual.

modelling_gaps.detail: Every slider is 0 to 10 or MIN to MAX on the panel. Only the oscillator and filter frequency sliders have marked physical scales, and those are decade marks rather than a stated law.
No times in seconds for attack, decay or release, so the TIME FACTOR multiplier has nothing to multiply. This is the largest single gap for anyone trying to make the model sound right.

No cutoff range in Hz, no resonance law, and no account of what distinguishes the 4012 from the 4072 beyond the garbled sentence in item 12. The two circuits differ audibly on real hardware; this file cannot say how.
FM inputs accept -10 V to +10 V and the PWM inputs work at 1 V per 10% duty, but no volts-per-octave figure is given for the FM path, so full-slider modulation depth is unknown.
The four ranges are described as overlapping and the panel marks one decade per division, but the actual span of each range is not given.
Described as a voltage multiplier with a -10 V to +10 V output. Whether it is a true four-quadrant multiplier, and how the AUDIO/DC switch changes the VCO1 path, is not stated.
COLOR is a continuous slider through low frequency, pink and white, but the spectral shape at intermediate positions is not described.
A digital emulation of a spring on this model and a real tank on the BLUE MARVIN. No decay time, no controls beyond left and right level, no statement of how the two differ.
No attack or release time constant and no transfer function from input amplitude to output voltage, only a maximum of +14 V.
Described qualitatively as slew on CV and low-pass on audio. No time constant range and no statement of whether it is linear or exponential slew.
Passive and unbuffered, so patching several sources together has real electrical consequences that a naive model will not reproduce.
Nothing anywhere on VCA headroom, filter saturation, or what happens when attenuator sliders are driven hard. On a 2600 these are much of the character.

The uploaded original manual is a 112-page scan with no text layer. Running OCR over it is the obvious next move: it is likely to settle the filter circuits, the envelope times, the keyboard CV scaling and the sync source.
